previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of hypercoagulable state, chronic anticoagulation with Lovenox, stable aortic arch thrombus, and chronic chest and abdominal pain was admitted for worsening pain. The chest pain was pleuritic in nature and non-cardiac, with normal cardiac enzymes and EKG. Abdominal pain was diffuse and severe, and on examination, a new incisional hernia was identified. Surgery recommended outpatient management. Pain was controlled with IV morphine initially, then transitioned to oral oxycodone with acetaminophen. The patient's hemoptysis and tracheobronchomalacia remained stable. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with surgery for hernia repair, continue all chronic medications, use temporary increased oxycodone for pain, and evaluate a persistent dental issue with a dentist.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with hemoptysis in the setting of factor V
Leiden deficiency and IVC filter.  Comes in with right lower quadrant
abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  Non-contrast CT of the abdomen from outside hospital from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  64-row MDCT obtained of the abdomen and pelvis from the lung bases
through to the proximal femora.  This study was done with IV and oral
contrast.  Coronal and sagittal displays reviewed alongside axial cuts.

FINDINGS:  The lung bases are clear with no evidence of pleural effusion,
focal consolidation, nodule, or mass.  The heart does not appear enlarged and
there is no pericardial effusion.

The liver enhances homogenously without any focal lesion.  The gallbladder is
normal.  The adrenals are normal bilaterally.  The kidneys enhance and excrete
contrast symmetrically and promptly.  There is a small hypodensity that is
difficult to assess in the prior film without contrast that measures 1.8 x 1.6
cm and does not enhance.  This most likely represents a benign renal cyst. The
pancreas is normal.  Intra-abdominal loops of large and small bowel are
unremarkable.  There is no bowel wall thickening or any signs of bowel
obstruction.  The abdominal aorta is unremarkable.  The celiac, SMA and ___
are both widely patent.  The SMV is patent as well.  Noted in the right upper
quadrant is a small incisional hernia containing omentum at known trocar site.
The neck of this hernia is approximately 1 cm.  A small right upper quadrant
incisional hernia is also appreciated on the film from ___ and is
unchanged.  The patient is status post splenectomy.  Prosthetic mesh seen
repairing ventral wall defect.  No evidence of adhesion of bowel to this mesh
repairing this ventral hernia.  There is no evidence of recurrence of hernia.
There are numerous subcutaneous lesions consistent with changes suggestive of
Lovenox injections.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:  The distal ureters are seen emptying into the
bladder bilaterally.  There is no evidence of ureteral stone.  The bladder is
partially distended with urine without any thickening of the bladder wall or
filling defects.  The prostate is unremarkable.  The seminal vesicles are
normal.  No inguinal or pelvic lymphadenopathy by CT criteria.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Right upper quadrant small incisional hernia containing omentum, unchanged
from CT from ___.
2.  No additional acute abdominal or pelvic process to account for the
patient's abdominal pain.

INDICATION:  Factor V Leiden deficiency, prior history of pulmonary embolism
and aortic thrombus.  Hemoptysis and tracheobronchomalacia demonstrated on a
bronchoscopy.  Please evaluate tracheobronchomalacia.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric multidetector CT acquisition of the trachea and chest
was performed without intravenous contrast at maximal inspiration and dynamic
forced expiration.  Two attempts were made at dynamic forced expiration as the
initial study did not show adequate decrease in airway caliber.  Images are
presented for display in the axial plane at 1.25-, 5- and 2.5-mm collimation
respectively.  A series of multiplanar reformation images were also submitted
for review.

FINDINGS:  There is no pathologic enlargement of the supraclavicular, axillary
or mediastinal lymph nodes.  The cardiac size is normal without evidence of
pericardial effusion.  There is no pleural effusion.  The central airways are
patent, there is no evidence of an intrabronchial lesion.  

There is no appreciable tracheal or bronchial collapse.  For example, at the
level of the lower trachea, the inspiratory transverse diameter is 314 mm2 and
this declines to 216 mm2 on the forced expiration.  There is no evidence of
airtrapping.  A 3-mm noncalcified solid nodule in superior segment of the
right lower lobe is stable since a comparable CT of ___.  Right lower lobe
atelectasis is mild.

The study is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation, only to confirm
mild hepatic steatosis and normal-appearing adrenals.  Lower thoracic spine
anterior osteophytosis is mild.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Tracheobronchomalacia is not demonstrated on the dynamic expiratory
maneuvers, despite two attempts by the patient.
2.  Incidental finding of 3-mm noncalcified superior segment right lower lobe
nodule, stable since ___.  In light of the history of smoking, a followup
CT is suggested in 12 months' time to assess for stability.
